finding.claim: Duplicate element ids let an attacker hide a <use> expansion bomb from the threshold check. Subjects are keyed by id with last-wins, so the browser's first-id element is never in the reference graph, and the decoy the sanitizer sees has zero uses.
finding.sink: Client-side renderer expanding <use> chains (exponential, DoS); bypasses useThreshold

trace.note: subjects[id] overwritten by later duplicate; first element dropped
processReferences only walks subjects, so first-copy <use> edges never added
findByElementId returns only the last-id subject
countUse() on decoy returns 0, so use is kept
use element passes isUseTagExceedingThreshold

finding.guards_checked: useThreshold (default 1000) and NestingException depth check both operate only on last-wins subjects; no duplicate-id rejection. Not executed: no shell tool available; based on code reading.

finding.claim: Normalizing xlink:HREF to xlink:href via setAttribute creates a non-namespaced attribute, so Helper::getElementHref no longer sees it and isUseTagDirty fails to flag an external <use> href.
finding.sink: Serialized output contains a live xlink:href referencing an external document; violates the internal-only <use> policy

trace.note: cleanXlinkHrefs runs on the element
isHrefSafeValue accepts https:// so value passes
removeAttribute('xlink:HREF') then setAttribute('xlink:href') creates no-namespace attribute
hasAttributeNS(XLINK, 'href') is false for no-namespace attribute
localName 'xlink:href' != 'href', so loop skips it; getElementHref returns null
isUseTagDirty returns false (null href), use kept

finding.guards_checked: Scheme allowlist (isHrefSafeValue) applied before normalization; isUseTagDirty applied after normalization but cannot see the renamed attribute. Browser cross-origin <use> restrictions may limit real-world impact (unverified). Not executed.

finding.claim: removeRemoteReferences(true) does not remove several remote-reference forms: unquoted url(), href attributes with https:// or //, and <style> text or non-wrapped style attributes containing url()/@import.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied SVG passed to Sanitizer::sanitize() with removeRemoteReferences enabled (svg-scanner.php:97)
finding.sink: Sanitized output that still triggers remote fetches (tracking, IP disclosure) when rendered

trace.note: removeRemoteReferences gate applies only to attributes in cleanAttributesOnWhitelist
regex requires a quote inside url(); unquoted url(https://...) returns false
href https:// and // allowed by isHrefSafeValue and never passed to hasRemoteReference
style element allowed; its text content is never inspected

finding.guards_checked: Option is opt-in; hasRemoteReference is applied to attribute values only, and only when the value is fully wrapped in url('...') with quotes. Low-severity hardening gap.

finding.claim: countUse() and hasInfiniteLoop() enumerate every path in the reference DAG without memoization, so a diamond ladder of depth 14 (about 2^14 paths) combined with ~10k <use> elements pointing at its top costs ~10^8 to 10^9 recursive calls per upload.
finding.source: Attacker-supplied SVG passed to Sanitizer::sanitize() (untrusted upload)
finding.sink: Server-side CPU exhaustion during sanitization (resource DoS); useThreshold is evaluated only after the full recursion

trace.note: isUseTagExceedingThreshold calls countUse() on each use target
countUse recurses over every use edge with no visited set or memo
hasInfiniteLoop recurses over every edge, bounded only by depth 15 not path count
useNestingLimit=15 bounds depth, so 2^14 paths pass without NestingException
each <use> triggers the full countUse before the threshold comparison

finding.guards_checked: useNestingLimit (depth only) and useThreshold (applied after full computation). No cap on path count or number of use elements. Timing estimate not measured; based on code reading.
